symptom: M10 report claimed factual half-life of 1126.83 Mb and skill half-life of 273.88 Mb yielding 4.11x ratio. However, empirical cloze knowledge baseline was 46% (half-life target 23%), which crossed at 217.40 Mb, while procedural skill baseline was 48% (half-life target 24%), which remained at 34% at 2-bit (140.85 Mb) and 40% at 1-bit (70.42 Mb). Skills never crossed the 24% target within the evaluated ladder. The 4.11x point estimate was an artifact of compute_half_life() checking absolute 0.50 accuracy.
detected_by: Adversarial Scientific Audit of Milestone M10 Report
root_cause: compute_half_life() evaluated absolute 0.50 accuracy rather than relative 50% baseline retention (A(B_half) = 0.50 * A_0). When transferred from synthetic universe (where A_0 = 1.0) to real LLMs (A_0 ~ 0.46-0.48), factual accuracies were all < 0.50, defaulting to 1126.83 Mb, and skill accuracies crossed 0.50 between 4b and 3b (273.88 Mb).
five_whys: Why 1: M10 reported a 4.11x ratio based on 1126.83 Mb vs 273.88 Mb crossing points.
Why 2: compute_half_life() returned the highest budget (1126.83 Mb) for facts because np.all(acc_sorted < 0.50) was triggered.
Why 3: The function tested absolute accuracy >= 0.50 instead of relative retention 0.50 * baseline_acc.
Why 4: In M7 synthetic universes, uncompressed accuracy was exactly 1.00, so absolute 0.50 equaled relative 50%.
Why 5: On real Pythia-70M, factual baseline is 0.460 (target 0.230, crossing at 217.40 Mb), while skill baseline is 0.480 (target 0.240, which is never crossed down to 2-bit or 1-bit).
fix: 1. Refactored compute_half_life() to compute true relative 50% baseline retention (A(B_half) = 0.50 * A_0) and return explicit bound information when uncrossed. 2. Empirically recomputed factual half-life crossing at 217.40 Mbits. 3. Proved that procedural skills stay above 24% down to 2-bit (34%) and 1-bit (40%), establishing a rigorous empirical lower bound B_half(skill) < 70.42 Mbits. 4. Replaced unsupported point estimate ratio 4.11x with rigorous lower bound Ratio > 3.09x >= 2.0x (or > 1.54x on 5-rung ladder). 5. Updated all reports, test assertions, and audit runner.
verification: pytest tests/ -v (75/75 passing); verified factual crossing 217.40 Mb and skill lower bound > 3.09x; audit runner green.

fix: Transparently report P_M11_6 as an empirical hardware baseline falsification under multi-threaded CPU execution; document that MLX compiled Metal graph achieves 140.7 tok/s (outperforming PyTorch MPS at 137.8 tok/s and multi-threaded CPU at 61.1 tok/s); document the dual benchmark (2.30x vs multi-threaded CPU, >4.5x vs single-threaded CPU).
